subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is the existing current-main guardrail set sufficient to close this billing/context issue after focused Windows fresh-session proof, or should maintainers require another source guardrail before close?
rationale: The code has multiple plausible fixes, but the remaining question is whether they prove the exact user-billing path or whether a high-impact provider-cost report needs stricter closure evidence.

options.title: Require focused proof before close
options.body: Run the fresh-session trajectory-sidecar proof on current main and close only if the model prompt/token payload stays isolated from old trajectory files.

options.title: Add another guardrail first
options.body: Keep this open for a targeted patch if proof shows any trajectory, memory-index, or reseed path still admits sidecar content into active model context.

options.title: Fold into broader defaults work
options.body: Treat this as partially covered by broader transcript-growth policy work, while preserving this issue as the canonical billing-path report until exact proof exists.

recommendation.title: Require focused proof before close
recommendation.body: Run the fresh-session trajectory-sidecar proof on current main and close only if the model prompt/token payload stays isolated from old trajectory files.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the trajectory/session artifact classifier cleanup that determines whether sidecars are treated as transcripts.
